subject: different DIC and WAIC values with different INLA versions

messages.author: f6d7dbf40606191a
messages.subject: different DIC and WAIC values with different INLA versions
parts:
Hello,

I used INLA for model selection to select between different Poisson regression models with mixed effects.
I ran the same code, on the same data set but for  3 different versions of INLA and I obtained 3 different values for WAIC and DIC.
The 3 versions are  23.9.9, 23.04.24, 22.12.16.

Did someone already notice such differences between versions? And with DIC/WAIC value should I trust?

Thank you in advance,

Nathalie

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] different DIC and WAIC values with different INLA versions
parts:
DIC and WAIC are examples of statistics compute that is a _sum_ and not
a _mean_, meaning that the 'numerical stdev' would be of order sqrt(n),
where n=#data. even a tiny change in the numerical optimisation can
manifest to a larger change in DIC and WAIC due to this.

newer versions of R-INLA, like the most recent testing version 24.01.09,
is way more accurate here than older versions, since quite a lot if
improvement has gone into making this more accurate and less depending
on stopping rules and paralellisations. like, the hyperparameter
optimisation is way more accurate for flat log posteriors.

here is an example with the current testing version

n=10^4
x=rnorm(n)
y=rpois(n, exp(1+x))

for(i in 1:5) {
print(inla(y ~ f(x), family="poisson",
data=data.frame(y,x),
control.compute=list(dic=TRUE))$dic$dic)
}

giving


[1] 46384.15761
[1] 46384.15591
[1] 46384.16554
[1] 46384.16591
[1] 46384.17613


(that was better than I expected...)



make sure you use R-4.3 and use the most recent testing version, that is
the best you can do.


Best
H
